original_question: For a periodic channel flow initially close to a monotone plane-parallel profile and containing a kink in one initial vorticity level set, show that the kink persists under Euler evolution and does not smooth out over time.
target_in_paper: Problem 23 in §8.2, 'Aging of the fluid, irreversibility and Lyapunov functions' (page 18), posed as a concrete instance of the broader Aging Problem in Problem 22. ([math.toronto.edu](https://www.math.toronto.edu/khesin/papers/Problems_in_GHD2205.01143.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the actual target phenomenon: a 2D Euler flow in a periodic channel, initial data near a plane-parallel profile, an initial vorticity level line with a kink, and the claim that this kink should persist rather than smooth out under time evolution. ([math.toronto.edu](https://www.math.toronto.edu/khesin/papers/Problems_in_GHD2205.01143.pdf))
missing_details: The paper specifies the exact domain as the periodic channel M = T × (0, a), with the first coordinate periodic; this should be stated explicitly in a stand-alone formulation. ([math.toronto.edu](https://www.math.toronto.edu/khesin/papers/Problems_in_GHD2205.01143.pdf))

The evolution is the 2D incompressible Euler equation ∂_t u + u·∇u = -∇p, div u = 0, with the velocity tangent to the boundary; your draft says 'Euler evolution' but does not spell out the governing equation or boundary condition. ([math.toronto.edu](https://www.math.toronto.edu/khesin/papers/Problems_in_GHD2205.01143.pdf))

The paper requires the initial velocity u0 to be C^1-close to the reference plane-parallel flow; the draft says only 'initially close' and omits the regularity of the closeness. The paper does not quantify this by an explicit ε. ([math.toronto.edu](https://www.math.toronto.edu/khesin/papers/Problems_in_GHD2205.01143.pdf))

The reference flow is not merely monotone: its scalar profile v = v(x2) must satisfy both v'(x2) > 0 and v''(x2) > 0 on (0, a). The draft captures monotonicity but omits the convexity condition v'' > 0. ([math.toronto.edu](https://www.math.toronto.edu/khesin/papers/Problems_in_GHD2205.01143.pdf))

The singular set is a level line of the initial scalar vorticity ω0 = curl u0, and the paper also assumes the nondegeneracy condition ∇ω0 ≠ 0 in M; this is missing from the draft. ([math.toronto.edu](https://www.math.toronto.edu/khesin/papers/Problems_in_GHD2205.01143.pdf))

To be fully stand-alone, the persistence claim should be attached to the corresponding vorticity level line under the forward Euler evolution ω(t, ·) = curl u(t, ·), since §8 frames these as long-time questions for 2D Euler flows. ([math.toronto.edu](https://www.math.toronto.edu/khesin/papers/Problems_in_GHD2205.01143.pdf))

The paper itself leaves the term 'kink' informal and places it in quotation marks, so a faithful rewrite should preserve that term rather than replace it with a sharper but newly invented notion. ([math.toronto.edu](https://www.math.toronto.edu/khesin/papers/Problems_in_GHD2205.01143.pdf))

No algebraic ambient ring/field, homogeneity, degree, or nilpotency conditions are relevant here; the hidden assumptions are geometric and analytic instead. ([math.toronto.edu](https://www.math.toronto.edu/khesin/papers/Problems_in_GHD2205.01143.pdf))
refined_question: Let M = T × (0, a), with T a one-dimensional torus, and let u(t, x) be a solution of the 2D incompressible Euler equations on M, with u tangent to ∂M. Assume that the initial velocity u0 is C^1-close on M to a plane-parallel flow u_ref(x1, x2) = (v(x2), 0), where v'(x2) > 0 and v''(x2) > 0 for every x2 in (0, a). Write ω(t, x) = curl u(t, x) for the scalar vorticity, assume that ∇ω0 ≠ 0 in M, and assume that one initial vorticity level line {ω0 = c} has a 'kink'. Show that, for every forward time t, the corresponding level line of ω(t, ·) still has a 'kink'; equivalently, the kink does not disappear as the fluid evolves in time. ([math.toronto.edu](https://www.math.toronto.edu/khesin/papers/Problems_in_GHD2205.01143.pdf))
justification: The draft is clearly aimed at Problem 23 in §8.2 because it matches the paper's exact ingredients: a periodic channel, initial data C^1-close to a plane-parallel profile with v' > 0 and v'' > 0, a nondegenerate initial vorticity foliation, and one vorticity level line with a 'kink', together with the requested conclusion that the kink persists in time. The surrounding paragraph places this as a concrete test case inside the broader Aging Problem (Problem 22), motivated by Yudovich's 'regularity deterioration' and by weak singularities that become sharper under evolution; §8 also explains that these are long-time questions for globally regular 2D Euler flows. To keep the rewrite paper-faithful and not broader than the source, I retained exactly this channel geometry and these hypotheses, and I used the nearby parallel-flow notation u_ref(x1, x2) = (v(x2), 0) from §6.2 as the cleanest paper-consistent way to spell out 'plane-parallel flow.' ([math.toronto.edu](https://www.math.toronto.edu/khesin/papers/Problems_in_GHD2205.01143.pdf))
